_why: Recorded runtimes for every CI job that claims a timeout under the shared-preamble floor.
A short timeout is a CLAIM that a job is cheap. Nothing checked the claim against the job's
actual runtime, so the claim could be false indefinitely: diff-check and mutation-targets both
carried 5m while needing 208-311s, and both died at the wall repeatedly (!1018, !1020, !1013).
The rule that was supposed to catch this keyed on which PREAMBLE a job used, not on how long
the job took, so trimming a preamble made a job compliant without making it fast.
This file is the evidence half. tests/test_ci_config.py asserts two things against it:
1. every job with a timeout below the floor HAS an entry here -- a new job cannot escape
the rule by simply not being listed, which is exactly how these two escaped;
2. its timeout is at least HEADROOM_FACTOR x its recorded runtime.
measured_s is wall-clock from a real CI job, not a local run and not an estimate. Record the
job id so the number can be audited. Re-measure when a job's work changes; a stale number
that is too LOW is the dangerous direction, because it makes a tight budget look safe.

diff-check.note: Was 208-309s until !1023 moved it off python:3.12-slim; the cost was apt installing git+make, never the diff gate itself.

resource-policy.note: before_script: [] -- the verifier imports only the stdlib, so nothing is installed.

mutation-targets.note: Was 302-311s on an idle runner; apt held 295 of the 300s. The remaining 66s is this job's own pip install, which it genuinely needs.

_why: Deadlines enforced INSIDE a job by a Makefile `timeout` wrapper, which a job's own `timeout:`
does not see. test-security shared TEST_FAST_DEADLINE=120 while its suite measured up to 95.5s
-- about 1.26x headroom -- and was killed at 89% complete on a contended runner (pipeline 9740,
job 110495). The `jobs` rule above could not catch it: that job's timeout was a comfortable
10m; the cap that fired was this inner one. Same contract as `jobs`: measured_s is a real CI
measurement with its job id, and the deadline must be at least headroom_factor x measured_s.

test-security.note: Slowest of four passing runs (83.2/94.2/94.7/95.5s), pytest's own reported duration for the security layer.
